generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, the goals you set shape how much you get from a module. A performance goal fixes on one mark, such as a grade for a single report. A mastery goal aims at a capability you will reuse across the degree, such as designing a sound study or evaluating evidence. Turning a vague aim into a mastery goal is what keeps your learning moving forward.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two psychology students set themselves a goal at the start of a new module.

Tom writes down a single aim: get at least 65 in the final research report. It is specific, but it is a performance goal fixed on one mark. When an early seminar task does not count towards that report, he puts little into it, and the goal gives no guidance on how to actually improve.

Amara starts with the same vague wish to do well, but rephrases it: get better at evaluating the evidence behind a psychological claim. That is a mastery goal, aimed at a capability rather than one mark. It guides every task on the module, counting or not, because each is a chance to practise the evaluation the goal names.

Both students set a goal. Only Amara's goal moved her learning forward across the whole module.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, goals come in two kinds: performance goals target a mark, while mastery goals build a capability, such as evaluating evidence, that lasts beyond one report. A vague aim is neither until you make it specific. You can now tell the two apart, rephrase a loose aim into a mastery goal, and set one of your own. With mindset, motivation and goals all working, you are ready to keep progressing.

check.body: In the worked example, what made Amara's goal move her learning forward where Tom's did not?

items.text: It aimed at a reusable capability, evaluating evidence, so it guided every task on the module.
It set a higher target mark than Tom's goal.
It was written down more neatly.
It focused only on the final report that counted.

feedback.correct: That's right. The mastery goal aimed at a capability, so it guided every task, counting or not.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what let Amara's goal guide work across the whole module.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara's goal moved learning forward because it aimed at a reusable capability and guided every task. The others stay fixed on a single mark.
